newsitem.title: INDIA: India govt securities rally on RBI's bank rate cut.
newsitem.headline: India govt securities rally on RBI's bank rate cut.

text.p: Indian securities rallied on Thursday following the central bank's decision on Wednesday to cut its bank rate and trigger an interest rate cut.
The 12.59 percent 2004 stock, which the RBI sold on tap on Wednesday at par with accrued interest, was traded at a premium of 15 to 20 paise, dealers said.
The decision to sell this stock at par had the market in a turmoil on Thursday.

The 12.14 percent 2000 stock rose to 101.50/62 rupees on Thursday from the previous close of 101 rupees, dealers said. The 12.5 percent 2004 stock was quoted at 100.0/100.20 rupees compared to Wednesday's traded price of 99.95 rupees.
The RBI cut the bank rate by one percentage point to 10.0 percent on Thursday.
Dealers said Thursday's rally was subdued because of firm overnight call money rates.
Prices are expected to firm up further on Saturday when return of repo money from the RBI to banks will swell bank coffers, dealers said.
Indian banks, flush with funds because of sizable growth in deposits and poor credit growth, have been investing heavily in securities in recent months.
